##### Source: Player's Handbook, [Carbon Pink](https://slimwiki.com/carbon-pink/the-elf-race), Neon City NightsThanks to Casters & Co.#6381 for the new control groups, and to reny#8234 for expanding on some of them!

In an effort to maintain their nepotistic control over the New World, corporations bankrolled the Extension of Life Functions program, a gene-editing project dedicated to keeping corporate directors, board members and vital employees alive for as long as possible, maintaining the status quo indefinitely. Executive Elfs are the direct descendants of the original board members that bankrolled the project, while Street Elfs are the result of Elfs breeding with humans. Undercity Elfs were bred to thrive in and maintain the interconnected underground datacenters under the megacities, and few ever make it up to the surface.

![Geo Albright, a male Elf (by Spliff)](https://neoncitylights.wdfiles.com/local--files/deleted:race:geo/muffindispersalservices.png)

### Roleplaying an Elf

Your lineage determines a lot about how you ended up needing to become an adventurer. What caused your Executive Elf to fall so far from the luxury and wealth of their ancestors? Which director mated with a human to create your Street Elf? Why has your Undercity Elf made it up to the surface?

No matter the reason, an adventuring Elf is rarely a happy Elf, and overtones of haughty disdain lace every word out of their mouths.

### Elf Naming Conventions

Executive Elfs, being the descendants of the upper crust of Old World society, tend to have very exuberant and fanciful family names. Street Elfs have lost touch with this tradition somewhat, and have simpler human first names to reflect that, but retain their societal family names. Undercity Elfs, being manufactured to serve in megacity datacenters, often only have first names.

Executive Elf names include Allegra Dankworth, Quincy Eastaughffe, Roderick Bisciotti, Arnault Bettencourt, Jae Ji-Yeong, Mars Plutarch, etc.

Street Elf first names include Mosie, Beth, Luca, Zion, Remi, Atlas, Mika, Theo, Zoe, Dante, Rhys, Giovanni, Ximena, etc.

Undercity Elf names include Kay, Jay, Ell, En, Que, Zed, Seven, Nine, Deejay, Opie, Abbie, Ceedie, Effigy, etc.

# Elf Features

- **Ability Score Increase.** Increase one ability score by 2, and increase a different one by 1, or increase three different scores by 1.
- **Age.** Elfs reach maturity at 18. Elfs can live centuries while maintaining a youthful appearance, some of the oldest nearing half a millennia.
- **Size.** Your size is Medium. Elfs are between 6 and 8 feet tall.
- **Speed.** Your base walking speed is 30 feet.
- **Duskvision.** You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light.
- **Born for the Boardroom.** You have advantage on saving throws you make to avoid the charmed condition on yourself, and can't be put to sleep by tech.
- **Computer Vision Syndrome.** You have advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the blinded condition on yourself, and on checks to see through visual deceptions.
- **Caffeinated Blood.** You can finish a long rest in 4 hours if you spend those hours in a semiconscious state, unaware of your surroundings.
- **Required Reading.** Whenever you make an Intelligence (History) check related to the origin of a corporate entity or modern business practice, you are considered proficient in the History skill and add double your proficiency bonus to the check, instead of your normal proficiency bonus.

## Extension of Life Function Control Groups

### Executive

Executive ELFs are direct descendants of the original board members who bankrolled the Extension of Life Functions program. They're often powerful CEOs, who view themselves superior and won't shy away from reminding you of your inferiority.

- **Compartmentalize.** When you are subject to an effect with the sole purpose of compelling or forcing you to act in a certain way, such as the *[command prompt](/tech:command-prompt)* tech, you can delay the effect on you for a turn. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.
- **Worked With IT.** You know one trick of your choice from the [Techwizard tech list](/techs:techwizard). Starting at 4th level, you know and can cast one first- or second-level tech of your choice from the [Techwizard tech list](/techs:techwizard) with this trait. Casting the tech with this trait doesn't require material components. Once you cast the tech with this trait, you can't cast the tech with it again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast this tech using tech slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your techcasting ability for these techs when you cast them with this trait (choose when you select this lineage).

### Street

Street ELFs are the result of ELFs breeding with humans. They often end up living in the poorer areas of Neon City, having lost touch with their ancestors and preferring to live quiet lives.

- **Speedy.** Your walking speed is increased by 5 feet.
- **Streetside Agility.** Your reflexes and agility allow you to move with a burst of speed. When you move on your turn in combat, you can double your speed until the end of the turn. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you move 0 feet on one of your turns.

### Undercity

Undercity ELFs were bred to thrive in and maintain the interconnected underground data centers of Neon City. Undercity ELFs rarely make it topside, which has often led to them developing a mistrust of anyone who lives in the wealthier districts, preferring to keep to themselves.

- **Nightvision.** You have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of grey.
- **Hunter in the Dark.** When attacking targets from a position of darkness, you gain advantage on attacks against them.

### Villa

A sub-lineage of Executive ELFs, Villa ELFs are known for their luxurious lifestyles and reside in high-end gated communities, inside wealthy Villas.

- **Hyperfixation.** You gain proficiency in your choice of Investigation or Insight. When you make a Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Insight) check, you can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to the ability check.
- **Survival of the Richest.** You know the *[light](/tech:light)* trick. Starting at 3rd level, you can cast the *[low power mode](/tech:low-power-mode)* tech with this trait. Starting at 5th level, you can cast the *[cloaking](/tech:cloaking)* tech (targeting yourself only) with this trait. Casting these techs with this trait doesn’t require material components. Once you cast either of these techs with this trait, you can’t cast that tech with it again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast these techs using tech slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your techcasting ability for these techs when you cast them with this trait (choose when you select this lineage).

### Serum

Serum ELFs are individuals who have undergone experimental genetic treatments, allowing them to harness the power of the nanites in their body to perform extraordinary feats. They are feared by many and coveted by others.

- **Thick Skin.** You have resistance to entropic damage.
- **Serum Surge.** As a bonus action, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Once you use this trait, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.
  - Starting at 3rd level, you also gain resistance to all damage when you teleport using this trait. The resistance lasts until the start of your next turn.
